clips.speaker: Donald Trump
clips.quote: Christians, get out and vote. Just this time. You won't have to do it anymore. Four more years, you know what? It'll be fixed. It'll be fine. You won't have to vote anymore, my beautiful Christians.
clips.cut_note: cut BEFORE 'I love you, Christians' (disputed transcription); don't merge with the later 'in four years' line
clips.rights: fair use (C-SPAN camera; expect Content ID claim; keep rationale)

clips.speaker: Gen. Mark Milley
clips.quote: We don't take an oath to a king, or queen, or a tyrant or a dictator. And we don't take an oath to a wannabe dictator.
clips.verify: take exact wording from DVIDS transcript/audio
clips.rights: public domain (DoD); DVIDS: add 'no endorsement implied'

clips.speaker: VP Mike Pence (R)
clips.quote: To those who wreaked havoc in our Capitol today, you did not win. Violence never wins. Freedom wins. And this is still the People's House.

clips.speaker: Rep. Liz Cheney (R)
clips.quote: There will come a day when Donald Trump is gone, but your dishonor will remain.
clips.rights: public domain (committee feed; use only her dais shot)

clips.speaker: Rep. John Lewis
clips.quote: The right to vote is precious--almost sacred. In a democratic society, it [is] the most powerful nonviolent instrument or tool that we have.

clips.speaker: Sen. Mitch McConnell (R)
clips.quote: There is no question--none--that President Trump is practically and morally responsible for provoking the events of the day.

clips.speaker: Lyndon B. Johnson
clips.quote: The vote is the most powerful instrument ever devised by man for breaking down injustice
clips.rights: likely public domain; confirm footage provenance (White House/Navy vs network)

clips.speaker: Ronald Reagan
clips.quote: 'We the People' tell the government what to do; it doesn't tell us.
clips.rights: public domain (White House footage via reaganlibrary.gov; avoid Foundation YouTube)
